parsed.explanation: The operative regime is a police-discretion system rather than a border-exclusion system. Same-sex criminalisation is rarely prosecuted, but it is the documented lever police use to harass, extort, assault and ignore LGBTQ complaints, including against trans people; forced anal/vaginal exams and birth-sex custody are documented. LGR and mixed public attitudes are climate signals, not visitor protections. A trans visitor outed at a police stop, hospital or detention faces serious state-tolerated harm with no effective remedy. No execution pathway is documented, keeping it above the 0.15 tier.

entry_documents.exposure: No border-specific trans document practice documented; same-sex and gender-expression laws could expose an outed visitor at official checks.
entry_documents.protection: None documented for foreign trans documents; the LGR circular is resident-facing.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch could trigger police scrutiny, but no documented border refusal pattern.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Police systematically harass and extort LGBTQ people, cite §365, ignore complaints; forced anal/vaginal exams are documented; detention risks birth-sex placement.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: LGR card may permit preferred-gender placement 'where possible'; no statutory rule; a visitor is unlikely to hold the card.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Outing at a police stop can escalate to extortion, forced exam, arrest and birth-sex custody.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Prisons have no dedicated trans housing; birth sex is the practical default; no statutory placement rule.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Case-by-case preference for cardholders where possible; doctor assessment for others.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: A foreign visitor without the local recognition card is likely assessed and placed by birth sex.

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming surgery and hormones are scarce; staff show ignorance, curiosity and ridicule; some avoid public hospitals.
care_services.protection: No anti-discrimination protection documented for trans visitors.
care_services.interaction: Emergency or routine care can expose identity with little recourse.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Police are identified as foremost perpetrators of LGBTI rights violations; §365 is used to justify harassment, assault and extortion; complaints are ignored.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Head of state and some public support exist, but no enforceable protection is documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Police discretion converts outing into state-tolerated abuse.

minors_guardians.exposure: No youth-specific findings; conversion therapy is not banned and families reportedly seek it; higher penalty applies to offences against under-16s.
minors_guardians.interaction: An adult with a minor may face scrutiny; an outed minor is vulnerable to family or medical intervention.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Police routinely ignore LGBTQ complaints, especially sexual violence or blackmail, citing §365; no hate-crime recourse.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Reporting violence can lead to further harassment or extortion.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No comprehensive anti-discrimination law; LGR circular is not law; current prosecution rate is unresolved; complaints are ineffective.
remedies_unknowns.protection: The national human rights commission facilitated a 2015 complaint; official acknowledgment exists.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are slow and discretionary and do not constrain police.

anchor_checks.comparison: Above 0.15-A: no documented capital application or routine months-long pretrial beatings, and prosecutions are described as limited. But police extortion, forced exams and birth-sex custody remain severe.

Slightly below 0.25-B: similar police extortion and threat-of-arrest pattern, but here §365 carries up to 10 years, forced anal/vaginal exams are documented, and prison placement defaults to birth sex.
Below 0.35-A: that anchor is exclusion and humiliation without imprisonment. Here an outed trans visitor faces arrest, forced exams and birth-sex custody, not merely removal.
Well below 0.55-B: administrative secondary screening and return transport versus systematic police abuse, a criminal statute, torture-adjacent exams and no working remedy.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is not primarily a border-exclusion system but a police-discretion system. Same-sex criminalisation is formally rarely prosecuted, yet it is the documented lever police use to harass, extort, assault and ignore LGBTQ complaints, including against trans people; forced exams and birth-sex custody are documented. LGR and mixed public attitudes are climate signals only. A visitor who is outed at a police stop, hospital or detention faces serious state-tolerated harm with no effective remedy. No execution pathway is documented, keeping it above the 0.15 tier.
